# heo cheatsheet: agents

For a program or an LLM calling heo. Prefer the machine-readable manifest to this page: it is the
same data. The prose behind each verb is in [commands](manual/commands.md); the roles are in
[authorization](manual/authorization.md).

## Discover

```sh
heo spec --format json                 # every verb: side effect, flags, examples, next steps
heo spec --version                     # the manifest schema version alone
heo spec coverage --min 100            # fails while a verb lacks a side-effect tier
heo adapter list --format json         # what each adapter in this build can do
heo channel get <channel> --format json   # which provider verbs a channel supports
```

Over REST the same list is `GET /v1/commands`; over MCP each verb is one tool, named by its path
joined with dots (`conversation.list`). Both list only what you may call.

## Rules

- Pass `--format json`. Parse stdout; errors are a JSON envelope on stderr with `code`, `message`,
  `suggested_fix` and `transience`.
- IDs are record IDs, as the listing printed them (`conv_123`, `msg_123`, `op_123`). Never build
  one.
- Preview before you write: every verb marked `dry-run` takes `--dry-run`, which prints the exact
  effect and writes nothing.
- Writes are uma operations. Pass `--idempotency-key` (or keep the one heo printed) so a retry
  replays instead of repeating. A write that returns `queued` is accepted, not delivered: follow it
  with `heo delivery get <operation>`.
- Exit 70: no daemon is running. Do not retry; a human runs `heo service start`.
- Exit 4 is a conflict (stale `--revision`, state moved): re-read, then decide. Exit 6 is
  transient: back off and retry. Exit 8 is `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`: the provider may have acted; `heo
  delivery reconcile <operation>`, never a blind resend.
- Exit 5 is a refusal: your role does not allow it, or a destructive verb has no `--confirm=yes`.
  Do not retry unchanged.
- Destructive verbs (`contact merge`, `message delete`, `storage restore`) are refused over REST,
  gRPC and MCP; the control socket runs them with `--confirm=yes`.
- A `plugin:` actor's write may be held (state `held`): only a person runs `heo operation held
  approve|edit|reject`; a plugin is refused, exit 5. Over MCP `held show|approve|edit|reject` name
  their operation with `--operation`.
- Streams (`event watch`, `task watch`, `operation watch`) are for a terminal or the socket: poll
  `event list --cursor` from a served surface.
- A hook plugin is any executable: an envelope in on stdin, a result of operations out on stdout.
  Try one with `heo hook test <plugin> --event <id>` before enabling it; see [write a
  plugin](manual/hooks.md#write-a-plugin-in-any-language).

## Exit codes

| Exit | Meaning | Retry |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | success | - |
| 1 | unclassified failure, or a schema newer than this binary | no, report |
| 2 | usage error, validation, or `UNSUPPORTED` by the channel's adapter | no, fix the call |
| 3 | not found | no |
| 4 | conflict: stale revision, owned store, daemon already running | re-read first |
| 5 | refused: no role, or destructive without `--confirm=yes` | no |
| 6 | transient | yes, with backoff |
| 8 | `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN`: the provider may have acted | reconcile, do not resend |
| 70 | no daemon is running | no, a human starts it |
